title: Two Grips, Each Wired to a Cable

scenes.visual: Show the title over a cell attached to an extracellular matrix mesh, with an integrin linking the mesh to an internal filament.

scenes.tts: Integrins connect cells to the extracellular matrix, the woven material cells secrete around themselves. Inside, they link to the cytoskeleton and send signals. So this grip lets a pull outside reach the cell's own filaments. Each integrin pairs an alpha subunit with a beta subunit. Many recognise R G D in fibronectin. Talin binds the beta tail and links it to actin. Vinculin reinforces the link. These complexes gather into focal adhesions beneath cultured cells.

scenes.visual: Open on a cell gripping a secreted matrix mesh. Highlight matrix, integrin and internal cytoskeleton in one continuous chain; show a pull reaching the filaments and a separate signal arrow entering the cell. Zoom to the alpha–beta pair binding fibronectin's RGD site. Build the beta-tail–talin–actin chain with vinculin reinforcing it. Zoom out to clusters labelled focal adhesions beneath a cultured cell. Remove the old integrin-family census.

scenes.tts: Not every integrin reaches actin. Hemidesmosomes pin basal skin cells to their basement membrane. Integrin alpha six beta four binds laminin three three two outside. Inside, it connects through plectin to keratin filaments.
scenes.narration: Not every integrin reaches actin. Hemidesmosomes pin basal skin cells to their basement membrane. Integrin α6β4 binds laminin-332 outside. Inside, it connects through plectin to keratin filaments.
scenes.caption: Not every integrin reaches actin. Hemidesmosomes pin basal skin cells to their basement membrane. Integrin α6β4 binds laminin-332 outside. Inside, it connects through plectin to keratin filaments.
scenes.visual: Place the actin-linked focal adhesion beside a hemidesmosome beneath a basal skin cell. Label the second chain laminin-332, integrin α6β4, plectin and keratin. Keep the basement membrane visible as the anchoring sheet.

scenes.tts: The other grip joins neighbouring cells. Cadherins need calcium to stiffen their outer arms. Remove calcium from cultured epithelial cells and they let go. Put it back and they knit together again.

scenes.visual: Widen from the matrix attachment to neighbouring epithelial cells. Highlight their cadherin contact. Remove calcium dots, let the arms go limp and cells separate; restore calcium and show the sheet re-forming.

scenes.tts: A classical cadherin crosses the membrane once and often binds the same kind on the next cell. Inside, beta-catenin binds its tail and recruits alpha-catenin, which couples the junction to actin. These contacts gather into adherens junctions.

scenes.visual: Build matching cadherins across two neighbouring membranes. Add β-catenin, α-catenin and actin inside each cell. Zoom out to a belt of contacts labelled adherens junction. Remove the old p120 branch from this scene.

scenes.tts: What does the matrix contribute? Collagen cables resist pulling. Elastic fibres stretch and recoil. Fibronectin makes networks that cells grip. Basement membranes are thin sheets built from linked laminin and type four collagen networks. Proteoglycans draw in water, forming gels that resist compression. Hyaluronan helps keep the matrix hydrated. The matrix also stores growth factors, which can be released when it is cut or pulled. It supplies mechanical support and biochemical cues.

scenes.visual: Show a matrix cutaway, highlighting each component as named: taut fibrillar collagen cables; elastic fibres stretching and recoiling; an integrin gripping a fibronectin network; a basement-membrane sheet of linked laminin and type IV collagen networks; and proteoglycans drawing water into a compression-resistant gel with hyaluronan. Finish with stored growth factors released from matrix when cut or pulled. Use labels for mechanical support and biochemical cues.

scenes.tts: Some of these connections also respond to force. A cell pulls on its adhesions with myosin two. Stretching purified talin exposes hidden vinculin-binding sites. In a reconstituted cadherin-catenin complex, some bonds to actin last longer under load, over a limited range. Matrix mechanics can also bias cell behaviour in culture. Adhesions connect the matrix and neighbouring cells to internal filaments, and some links change when pulled.
